item.title: Südzucker posts stable first-half sales as biofuel demand offsets low sugar prices
item.description: Europe's largest sugar producer Südzucker's reported broadly unchanged sales for the first half of its financial year on Thursday, as strong demand for biofuels partly offset lower revenue from sugar and starch products.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Europe's largest sugar producer Südzucker's (SZUG.DE) reported broadly unchanged sales for the first half of its financial year on Thursday, as strong demand for biofuels partly offset lower revenue from sugar and starch products. The average EU white sugar price fell to €499 a metric ton in July, its lowest level since August 2022, European Commission data showed. Südzucker posted half-year revenue of €4.19 billion ($4.69 billion), compared with €4.20 billion a year ago It said droughts and low rainfall since June had led to a substantial decline in expected beet yields The company had [USN:L8N45K0DX TEXT:"pre-released"] half-year earnings and raised its outlook in September, citing higher biofuel sales ($1 = 0.8925 euros)

item.title: USA-Les responsables de la Fed divisés sur la justification de la hausse des taux-"minutes"
item.description: Les responsables de la Réserve fédérale (Fed) ont divergé le mois dernier sur le raisonnement justifiant de relever les taux d'intérêt, certains d'entre eux notant la nécessité de contrer le choc énergétique tandis que d'autres, plus conservateurs, ayant dit avant tout vouloir lutter contre l'inflation.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les responsables de la Réserve fédérale (Fed) ont divergé le mois dernier sur le raisonnement justifiant de relever les taux d'intérêt, certains d'entre eux notant la nécessité de contrer le choc énergétique tandis que d'autres, plus conservateurs, ayant dit avant tout vouloir lutter contre l'inflation. D'après le compte-rendu publié mercredi de la réunion des 15-16 septembre de la Fed, lors de laquelle la banque centrale américaine a voté à l'unanimité pour [USN:L8N4581JU TEXT:"une hausse des taux"] de 25 points de base, ses membres ont débattu de la logique de ce resserrement monétaire. L'idée que la mesure soit avant tout une précaution a été mise en avant par "certains" responsables, est-il indiqué, quand d'autres se sont interrogés sur la perspective que ce relèvement des taux marque le début d'un cycle de resserrement monétaire. "De nombreux participants ont souligné qu'un relèvement de l'objectif des taux serait prudent pour gérer les risques, fournir des garanties contre l'inflation qui demeure de manière persistante au-dessus de l'objectif en raison d'une demande plus solide qu'attendu", est-il écrit dans les 'minutes'. Toutefois, d'autres responsables de la Fed ont dit voir la hausse des taux approuvée le mois dernier comme une mesure importante pour empêcher principalement le choc énergétique d'avoir de larges répercussions sur les prix. Selon le compte-rendu de la réunion, "plusieurs participants ont dit considérer la politique actuelle des taux comme non-restrictive ou légèrement restrictive seulement". "La plupart des participants ont établi qu'une hausse supplémentaire (...) sera vraisemblablement appropriée d'ici la fin de l'année", est-il ajouté dans le document.

item.title: 街角景気は9月は0.6ポイント上昇、秋物・大型連休が支え 住宅関連には金利上昇の影響も
item.description:
Kentaro Sugiyama
［東京 ８日 ロイター］ - 内閣府が８日に発表した９月の景気ウオッチャー調査で現状...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
街角景気は9月は0.6ポイント上昇、秋物・大型連休が支え　住宅関連には金利上昇の影響も 14:17 配信

２０２０年４月、都内で撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

Kentaro Sugiyama

［東京　８日　ロイター］ - 内閣府が８日に発表した９月の景気ウオッチャー調査で現状判断ＤＩは４７．０となり、前月から０．６ポイント上昇した。５カ月連続のプラスとなった。秋物の衣料品販売や大型連休中の集客が支えになったとの声が出た一方、住宅関連からは金利上昇の影響が出始めているとの指摘もあった。

内閣府は、ウオッチャーの景気の見方を「持ち直しの動きがみられる」で据え置いた。

指数を構成する３部門では、家計動向関連が前月から１．３ポイント上昇し４６．８となった。回答者からは「秋への移行が順調で、秋物が好調に推移している」（東北＝衣料品専門店）、「大型連休のおかげで売り上げが非常に伸びた。また、連休が長かったため遠方からの客も多かった（甲信越＝観光型旅館）といったコメントが寄せられた。

一方、住宅関連では「住宅ローン金利の上昇や、建築費、住宅価格の高止まりなどで、住宅取得に対する消費者の慎重な姿勢が強まっている（近畿＝その他住宅［展示場］）との声も聞かれた。

雇用関連は０．２ポイント上昇し４９．０となった。一方、企業動向関連は４７．１と、前月から１．１ポイント低下した。「資材価格や人件費の上昇が利益を圧迫してきている」（四国＝建設業）という。

２─３カ月先の景気の先行きに対する判断ＤＩは、前月から０．９ポイント低下の４７．４。６カ月ぶりマイナスとなった。

回答者からは「金利の上昇や車両価格の値上がりなど買い控えになる要素がある」（北関東＝乗用車販売店）、「各地での自然災害発生による旅行控えが起こると、今後の受注に悪影響を及ぼす」（沖縄＝レンタカー）といった声が上がった。

内閣府は先行きについて「中東情勢による不透明感が残ることに加え、自然災害の影響に対する懸念もみられるが、持ち直しの動きが続くとみられる」とした。

調査期間は９月２５日から３０日。

＊内閣府の発表資料は以下のＵＲＬでご覧になれます。

item.title: クレメンス氏に大統領自由勲章、トランプ氏表明 元サイ・ヤング賞投手
item.description:
Daniel Trotta
[７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Daniel Trotta

[７日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は７日、米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）の元投手ロジャー・クレメンス氏に、民間人に対する最高位の栄誉である大統領自由勲章を授与すると明らかにした。テキサス州での政治集会で表明した。

トランプ氏の友人でゴルフ仲間としても知られるクレメンス氏は、ＭＬＢ史上屈指の名投手の一人で、リーグ最優秀投手に贈られるサイ・ヤング賞を史上最多の７度受賞した。しかし、禁止薬物の使用疑惑を理由に、記者投票による野球殿堂入りには選出されていない。

トランプ氏は、クレメンス氏がなぜ殿堂入りを拒まれているのかと疑問を呈し、その埋め合わせとして勲章を授与すると述べた。クレメンス氏は壇上で「とにかく驚いている」とし、この賞をもらうのであればトランプ氏から受け取りたいと語った。

クレメンス氏は薬物使用を一貫して否定。２００８年の議会証言を巡り、偽証や議会妨害など計６件の罪で起訴されたが、一審は検察による不適切な証拠提出で審理が無効となり、やり直し裁判では陪審が全６件で無罪評決を下した。

item.title: India denies bias in satellite internet approvals after Musk's 'oligarchs' jab
item.description: India defended its satellite internet approval process as fair and non-discriminatory on Thursday, hours after billionaire Elon Musk accused unnamed "oligarchs" of blocking Starlink's launch in the South Asian nation.
item.dc:creator: Munsif Vengattil
item.content:encoded: India defended its satellite internet approval process as fair and non-discriminatory on Thursday, hours after billionaire Elon Musk accused unnamed "oligarchs" of blocking Starlink's launch in the South Asian nation. Starlink was being blocked by "certain oligarchs in order to maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people," Musk wrote on X, without naming anyone. India's telecom market is dominated by billionaires Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Jio and Sunil Mittal's Bharti Airtel. Their satellite internet ventures, alongside Musk's Starlink, have secured early approvals to launch in India but are awaiting spectrum assignment and final clearances. Airtel and Jio did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The wait has stretched on for four years for Starlink, following scrutiny over security requirements and access to spectrum. Responding to Musk's comments, India's telecommunications ministry said three entities were at broadly the same regulatory stage, with security assessments under way for each. It did not name the companies or Musk. "The suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived," the ministry said in a statement. The clash is not new. Musk has previously been [USN:L4N38E0RQ TEXT:"at odds"] with Mittal and Ambani over how India should grant them spectrum, before the three [USN:L4N3PV05S TEXT:"set aside"] their differences in 2025 to sign separate deals to distribute Starlink devices in India. India offers Starlink, part of Musk's SpaceX, access to a satellite broadband market that Deloitte has forecast will be worth $1.9 billion by 2030. The timing adds a diplomatic layer: the US has pushed Starlink's market access as a goodwill marker in trade talks with tariff-hit countries, and New Delhi and Washington [USN:L4N45S0BG TEXT:"have struggled"] to finalise a trade deal since reaching a framework in February. Security concerns have also followed the recovery of Starlink equipment in India. Indian authorities have said they found Starlink devices in two separate operations in late 2024: a drug seizure by police in the Andaman and Nicobar islands and an army search in Manipur state. Musk then said Starlink's satellite beams were "turned off over India" and were "never on in the first place", a remark he repeated on Wednesday.

item.title: POINT MARCHÉS Wall Street en repli, les rendements obligataires pèsent
item.description: La Bourse de New York a fini en baisse mercredi, au lendemain de records du S&P-500 et du Nasdaq, alors que les rendements des bons du Trésor américain à échéance longue ont repris leur progression et ravivé les craintes des investisseurs à propos de l'inflation et de l'ampleur de la dette.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Culp, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: La Bourse de New York a fini en baisse mercredi, au lendemain de records du S&P-500 et du Nasdaq, alors que les rendements des bons du Trésor américain à échéance longue ont repris leur progression et ravivé les craintes des investisseurs à propos de l'inflation et de l'ampleur de la dette. L'indice Dow Jones (.DJI) a cédé 0,66%, ou 341,11 points, à 51.180,17 points. Le S&P-500 (.SPX) , plus large, a perdu 17,18 points, soit 0,22%, à 7.801,75 points. Le Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) a reculé de son côté de 61,19 points (0,22%) à 27.538,69 points. Le Nasdaq finit dans le rouge pour la première fois en six séances, tandis que le S&P-500 et le Nasdaq voient leur série de quatre séances dans le vert s'arrêter. Après avoir reculé mardi, les prix du pétrole ont rebondi, le Brent ayant brièvement dépassé le seuil des 100 dollars le baril. Parallèlement, le rendement des bons du Trésor américain à 30 ans s'est établi à un pic de 24 ans. Dans un contexte de guerre prolongée entre les Etats-Unis et l'Iran, les préoccupations sur l'approvisionnement en pétrole ont provoqué une flambée des prix énergétiques, ce qui alimente les craintes à propos de pressions inflationnistes plus larges et par conséquent d'un cycle durable de resserrement monétaire. En y ajoutant les niveaux élevés de la dette des entreprises et de la dette publique américaine, la situation a provoqué ces dernières semaines des secousses sur les marchés financiers. Les investisseurs espéraient "un peu de répit avec le pétrole, qui aurait permis un peu de répit avec les taux et aurait donc aidé le marché boursier", a commenté Thomas Martin, gestionnaire de portfolio chez GLOBALT, à Atlanta. Notant que "le troisième trimestre était supposé être le plus faible de l'année" avec pour effet une correction sur les marchés, mais que cela ne s'était "pas produit", il a déclaré que les investisseurs en profitaient pour prendre des bénéfices. Les principaux indices de Wall Street ont effacé en fin de séance une partie de leurs pertes initiales après que l'Agence internationale de l'énergie (AIE) a annoncé vouloir accélérer la libération de réserves de pétrole, en priorité de diesel, ce qui a provoqué une baisse des prix du brut. Par ailleurs, le compte-rendu de la réunion de septembre de la Réserve fédérale (Fed), publié dans l'après-midi, montre des divisions parmi les responsables de la banque centrale américaine à propos de la logique justifiant de relever les taux, bien qu'a été décidée à l'unanimité la hausse du coût de l'emprunt opérée le mois dernier. Certains participants ont dit voir une hausse des taux comme nécessaire pour se prémunir des répercussions du choc énergétique, tandis que d'autres ont souligné vouloir lutter contre l'inflation alimentée par la solidité de la demande. D'après des données FedWatch de CME, les marchés financiers misent actuellement à environ 17% à peine sur l'hypothèse d'une nouvelle baisse des taux lors de la réunion d'octobre de la Fed, contre plus de 37% une semaine plus tôt. "Il y a toujours l'anticipation de hausses des taux supplémentaires, mais pas forcément à chaque réunion, et c'est ce que dit le marché: octobre sera une pause", a déclaré Thomas Martin. A noter, mercredi, le secteur des semiconducteurs, parmi les catalyseurs de Wall Street cette année, a fini en baisse de 1,2%. Parmi les secteurs majeurs du S&P-500, les soins de santé (.SPXHC) ont enregistré les gains les plus importants. A l'inverse, l'industrie (.SPLRCI) a subi la plus forte baisse. SpaceX (SPCX.O) a cédé 2,5% après des informations de presse selon lesquelles le groupe détenu par Elon Musk désirait obtenir 40 milliards de dollars de financements en vue de l'acquisition de puces de Nvidia. Pour d'autres informations, veuillez cliquer sur les codes suivants: NYSE Nasdaq Résumé synthétique du marché...... (.AD.N) ..... (.AD.O) 25 plus forts volumes............. (.AV.N) ..... (.AV.O) Plus fortes hausses en %.......... (.PG.N) ..... (.PG.O) Plus fortes baisses en %.......... (.PL.N) ..... (.PL.O) Guide des indices boursiers américains.... item.title: Oilers erase early deficit with 5-goal second period, down Ducks
item.description: Leon Draisaitl had four assists to lead a huge second period in the Edmonton Oilers' 5-2 road win over the Anaheim Ducks on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Leon Draisaitl had four assists to lead a huge second period in the Edmonton Oilers' 5-2 road win over the Anaheim Ducks on Wednesday. Down 2-0 at the first intermission, Edmonton stormed back with five unanswered goals in the second frame. It was another strong offensive showing for the 3-0-1 Oilers, who have 22 goals in their first four games of the season. Evan Bouchard had two goals and an assist, and Connor McDavid produced a goal and two assists. Bouchard leads the NHL with six goals, while McDavid tops the league in assists (nine) and points (12). Draisaitl is up to nine points (three goals, six assists) after the star forward's 12th career game with at least four assists. Kasperi Kapanen and Vasily Podkolzin scored the Oilers' other goals. Devon Levi stopped 29 of 31 shots to earn his third win in as many starts this season. Beckett Sennecke scored two power-play goals for the Ducks, who fell short after winning their previous two games this season. Leo Carlsson had two assists. Lukas Dostal allowed five goals on 17 shots over two periods of action. Backup goalie Ville Husso replaced Dostal at the second intermission, and Husso stopped both shots faced. The Ducks got off to a dominant start by outshooting Edmonton 16-6 in the first period, and Sennecke struck twice with the extra attacker. Carlsson assisted on both tallies, but he also provided accidental help on Edmonton's first goal. Just 11 seconds into the second period, Bouchard's point shot deflected off Carlsson and beat a screened Dostal. The fortunate bounce set the tone for the Oilers' second-period surge. Kapanen struck next on the power play at the 6:30 mark, as the forward buried a one-timer for his 100th career NHL goal. Bouchard launched a big shot from the upper slot that beat a screened Dostal again to put the Oilers ahead at 14:12 of the second frame. A brilliant stretch pass from Draisaitl found Podkolzin entering the Ducks' zone 16:49 into the second period, and Podkolzin converted the breakaway goal. McDavid added the final blow by scoring with 52 seconds remaining before intermission. --Field Level Media

item.title: マドゥロ氏夫妻、米で追起訴へ 拘束した米国人拷問の罪で
item.description:
Andrew Goudsward Luc Cohen
[ワシントン ７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Andrew Goudsward　Luc Cohen

[ワシントン ７日 ロイター] - 米当局者は７日、米国で麻薬密輸の罪で起訴されているベネズエラのマドゥロ大統領と妻のシリア・フロレス氏について、同国で拘束された米国人を拷問した罪で８日にも追起訴される見通しだと明らかにした。

マドゥロ氏夫妻は１月、首都カラカスの自宅で米軍に拘束され、麻薬密輸の罪でニューヨークに移送された。公判は２０２７年６月１日に始まる予定で、両氏は無罪を主張している。マンハッタンの連邦検察の報道官はコメントを控えた。

拷問を受けたとされる被害者の身元など、起訴内容の詳細は明らかになっていない。

マドゥロ氏の在任中に不当拘束されたと米政府が認定した米国人には、汚職容疑で逮捕された石油会社幹部５人が含まれる。５人は２０２２年、米国で麻薬密輸の罪で有罪判決を受けたフロレス氏のおい２人との交換で解放された。

その他、失敗したマドゥロ政権転覆作戦に関連し、元米陸軍特殊部隊員２人が２０年にベネズエラで逮捕されていた。２人は２３年、別の身柄交換の一環として解放された。

マドゥロ氏の拘束後は、同氏の下で副大統領を務めたロドリゲス氏がベネズエラを率いており、トランプ米政権との協力を強化している。

マドゥロ氏（６３）とフロレス氏（６９）は、ニューヨーク・ブルックリンの連邦拘置施設に収容されている。

item.title: US, Russia explore gas sale to Europe amid Ukraine war, say sources
item.description: Top Russian and US officials, including Special Envoy Jared Kushner, have held talks about bringing a US investor into the Nord Stream pipelines that delivered gas to Germany before Russia invaded Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: John O'Donnell, Gram Slattery, David Gauthier-Villars
item.content:encoded: Top Russian and US officials, including US Special Envoy Jared Kushner, have held talks about bringing a US investor into the Nord Stream pipelines that delivered gas to Germany before Russia invaded Ukraine, five people with knowledge of the situation said. The discussions included Kirill Dmitriev, a close adviser to Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Kushner, the son-in-law of US President Donald Trump, the people said. Kushner, who has been trying to [USN:S0N44202E TEXT:"broker a truce"] between Russia and Ukraine, views doing business as central to restoring peace. Such a deal would enable US investors to profit from energy flows to Europe once the war ends. Dmitriev and Kushner have met in [USN:S0N42Q04U TEXT:"Moscow"] and [USN:L8N45F1PK TEXT:"New York"] in recent weeks. While it was unclear to what degree they discussed Nord Stream on those occasions, the topic remains on the agenda, two of the people told Reuters. "Any deals will have to be negotiated by Russia with DFC (US International Development Finance Corporation) and Treasury and must benefit United States taxpayers and companies," a White House official said, when asked about the pipeline discussions. There had been "no Nord Stream discussions recently", the official told Reuters. Dmitriev, who has campaigned for a resumption of Russian gas sales to Germany, met last month with US Energy and Treasury Department representatives [USN:S0N42Q04U TEXT:"to discuss potential US-Russia energy initiatives"]. A representative for Dmitriev declined to comment. It remains unclear how interested Washington is in pursuing the restarting of Russian gas flows to Germany, which is Europe's biggest energy consumer. A US official said that given the obstacles, a deal is unlikely in the medium term. The Nord Stream gas pipelines are sanctioned by the US and the EU, making any restart illegal. Trump could waive or soften US sanctions, but if Democrats win control of Congress in next month's midterm elections, this would become harder. Germany and other European countries, which are spending billions of euros rebuilding their military to defend themselves from Russia, would strongly resist reopening Nord Stream. A spokeswoman for Germany's economy and energy ministry said Nord Stream and Russian gas were sanctioned in Europe and that Germany had found alternatives. She said any reopening of the pipelines required government approval and this was not desired. Before Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Germany bought more than half of its gas from Russia through the two [USN:L8N3UD0YM TEXT:"Nord Stream"] pipelines. They were mothballed after Moscow throttled supply to Europe and were blown up in a series of underwater explosions in September 2022. NORD STREAM OWNERSHIP HURDLES Talks between Moscow and Washington are taking place against a backdrop of deep European mistrust of Russia's motives. Earlier this year, the heads of five European spy agencies told Reuters that Russia did not want to end the war quickly and [USN:L1N3ZD0IY TEXT:"was using US talks"] to push for business deals instead. Relations between Russia and Germany, which is among the biggest providers of military support to Ukraine, have hit a low ebb, as officials in Berlin have accused Russia of mounting a systematic campaign of [USN:L8N44T1N2 TEXT:"hybrid attacks"]. Some German lawmakers say that business deals would bolster Moscow as it pursues war with Ukraine. "This threatens to be a dirty deal that will cost Europe dearly," said Michael Kellner, a lawmaker who was in charge of German energy policy in the aftermath of the Ukraine invasion. "Americans and Russians will share the profits," he said. While Germany's coalition government is opposed to restarting the pipeline, Alternative for Germany (AfD), the country's most popular political party, [USN:L8N43103Q TEXT:"wants to do so"]. [USN:L8N4591QO TEXT:"Dmitriev will meet the AfD leadership"] early next year to discuss selling Russian gas again. But selling ownership of the company that controls the Nord Stream gas pipelines to a US investor or restarting Russian gas faces hurdles. The company is 51% owned by Russian state energy giant Gazprom, with a further 31% split between two German entities and the rest in the hands of a French and a Dutch firm. The two German shareholders are seeking to keep their shares to maintain German influence, should Gazprom sell its stake, said another person. Days after the Moscow meetings, Kushner said in Kyiv he had spoken to European counterparts about how the war pushed up energy prices, advocating "prosperity agreements" to encourage peace and give "leaders ... something to look forward to". While a gas deal would please the Kremlin, it would split German public opinion, which is divided over buying Russian energy, and Europe, where Poland and the Baltic states are particularly vulnerable to Russia and reject energy ties. Poland's political leadership is watching the discussions to reopen the pipeline but remains firmly opposed, said one person with knowledge of the government's thinking. Kushner and Dmitriev have also been discussing the sale of a collection of businesses, from oil refineries to petrol stations in Europe and elsewhere which are owned by Russian energy company Lukoil, said two other people familiar with the matter. Under that plan, a consortium of the DFC federal investment agency and investors from Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, would buy the assets, while US authorities would lift sanctions, those people said. "On Lukoil, Steve (Witkoff) and Jared (Kushner) worked with DFC to negotiate a substantial upfront payment and profits interest for the United States," said a White House official. Lukoil and Gazprom did not respond to requests for comment.

item.title: Japanese PM Takaichi's campaign to shed reflationist image needs substance behind the speeches
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's administration is ramping up efforts to shed its growth and easy money image through changes in rhetoric, a move that may backfire unless it is met with action such as substantial cuts to spending.
item.dc:creator: Leika Kihara, Makiko Yamazaki
item.content:encoded: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's administration is ramping up efforts to shed its growth and easy money image through changes in rhetoric, a move that may backfire unless it is met with action such as substantial cuts to spending. With major economies facing increased scrutiny from bond investors worried about rising inflation and yields, a lack of clarity on funding could cause another bond selloff in Japan given its $7 trillion debt pile that is the biggest among advanced nations. Takaichi vowed to cap new debt issuance around 40 trillion yen ($253 billion), even as spending requests for next year's budget hit a record 143 trillion yen. A planned two-year sales tax cut would also cost roughly 4 trillion yen per year. The government hopes to fill the gap by tapping rising tax revenues and state funds, a tricky task that would still pump money and inflationary pressures into the economy, analysts say. "Markets look at the substance of policy and won't believe words alone," said Eiji Doke, chief bond strategist at SBI Securities. "It's not that market players misunderstand Takaichi's policies. Rather, what they're watching is completely different from what the administration is trying to do." Takaichi became premier in October last year with a pledge to ramp up spending to spur growth. She filled government panels with her reflationist aides to promote loose fiscal policy. "Only by strengthening the economy would Japan achieve fiscal sustainability," she said in a policy speech back then in explaining her plan to compile a big spending package. The administration's hefty fuel subsidies, a tax-cut pledge and big investment plans cemented market perceptions of its policies being reflationary as the economy struggled to recover from decades of low growth and low inflation. But rising bond yields have become constraints on Takaichi's ambitions, forcing her administration to change its language. "Fiscal sustainability is a prerequisite in pursuing our 'responsible and proactive' fiscal policy," Takaichi told parliament on Monday, a sharp shift from her promise a year ago to prioritise growth over fiscal discipline. She also pledged to "control" bond issuance and enhance communication with markets in a sign of the administration's sensitivity to rising Japanese government bond (JGB) yields. The benchmark 10-year JGB yield has hit multi-decade highs on concern Takaichi's spending plans may lead to increased debt issuance and strain Japan's worsening finances. MEET WORDS WITH ACTION Efforts to phase out the administration's reflationist image geared up after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's calls in [USN:L1N44R07D TEXT:"August"] for Japan to depart from Abenomics - a mix of loose fiscal and monetary steps deployed by former premier Shinzo Abe to beat deflation. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama led the communication shift. In a [USN:P8N3KU036 TEXT:"recent"] media interview, she said the government decided around late August to recalibrate its messaging to reassure markets Takaichi was not pursuing reflationary policies. Soon after, reflationist aides began to change tone. Economy Minister [USN:L1N45H01I TEXT:"Minoru Kiuchi"], for one, said on September 25 the phase of Abenomics-style reflationary policies was over. Former Bank of Japan Deputy Governor Masazumi Wakatabe, another aide who sits on a government panel, also said last month reflationist policies "have no place in Japan now." The shift in tone occurred at the BOJ, too. Ayano Sato, a reflationist board member picked by Takaichi, told [USN:L1N45S130 TEXT:"Kyodo News "] on Wednesday that she supports raising rates. The government began to stress its spending plans are aimed at boosting supply capacity rather than reflating growth. Markets are focusing on whether Takaichi will meet words with action as the government drafts next fiscal year's budget. To be sure, robust corporate profits and inflation will likely lead to an increase in nominal tax revenues, which some analysts estimate will hit 90 trillion yen next year. Katayama vowed to tap unused funds and identify wasteful spending to seek revenues under Japan's equivalent of the US Department of Government Efficiency initiative, with a focus on the 7 trillion yen pooled by about 200 state funds. But tapping such funds for spending is unsustainable and could stimulate the economy, running counter to the BOJ's efforts to curb inflation with rate hikes, some analysts say. Former BOJ board member Asahi Noguchi, himself known as a reflationist, said now was the time to avoid boosting demand and causing bond yield rises that crowd out private investment. "The administration probably didn't have a coherent view, with some clinging to the legacy of Abenomics, though that seems to have changed," he said. "The key is to cut wasteful spending and convince markets Japan is serious about fiscal reform." ($1 = 157.9800 yen)

item.title: Vietnam police arrest 12 over theft of 2,700 cats for slaughter
item.description: Police in Vietnam have arrested 12 people accused of stealing 2,700 cats and selling them for slaughter in Ho Chi Minh City, the Ministry of Public Security said this week.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Police in Vietnam have arrested 12 people accused of stealing 2,700 cats and selling them for slaughter in Ho Chi Minh City, the Ministry of Public Security said this week. The suspects, aged between 16 and 39, were arrested on suspicion of stealing the cats with the intention of selling them for food. The men were found with cat traps, cages and fur-removal equipment, according to a ministry statement Police rescued dozens of cats during the raid Cat meat dishes are still served in some parts of Vietnam, particularly in rural areas, where they are sometimes marketed as "mini tiger" and believed by some consumers to have medicinal properties The arrests followed complaints from residents about the nighttime disappearance of their pet cats, the statement said. Authorities identified Luu Thanh Binh, 39, as the alleged ringleader and distributor. Investigators said he also bought live cats and resold them to customers seeking cat meat To supply the operation, Binh allegedly worked with several accomplices who recruited younger people to capture cats in residential neighbourhoods. Police said he also supplied traps used in the thefts The group operated mainly between 11 p.m. and 4 a.m., using fish bait and traps placed outside homes with pet cats. Captured animals were quickly collected and transported for sale, police said Police have returned 13 of the cats to their owners and said the remaining animals were being cared for by animal welfare group HavePaws while authorities continued efforts to identify their owners

item.title: 国債発行額は25年度同様に抑える、リフレ政策必要ない＝高市首相
item.description:
Yoshifumi Takemoto
［東京 ８日 ロイター］ - 高市早苗首相は８日の衆院代表質問で、２０２７年度の...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
国債発行額は25年度同様に抑える、リフレ政策必要ない＝高市首相 14:00 配信

10月5日、国会で所信表明演説を行う高市早苗首相。 REUTERS/Kim Kyung-Hoon

Yoshifumi Takemoto

［東京　８日　ロイター］ - 高市早苗首相は８日の衆院代表質問で、２０２７年度の予算編成での国債発行額について、補正予算後も前年を下回る４０兆円程度とした２５年度と「同様の取り組みを行う」と述べた。チームみらいの古川あおい議員への答弁。

＜電力・ガス補助金、原油価格等注視し適切に対応＞

１０月検針分で終了する電気・ガス料金の補助を巡り「冬を迎える家計への追加支援については原油や液化天然ガス（ＬＮＧ）価格の変動が与える影響を注視した上で適切に対応する」と述べた。参政党の豊田真由子議員への答弁。

国民民主党の玉木雄一郎代表に対する答弁では、「日本経済は物価が持続的に下落する意味でのデフレではない」とし、「リフレ政策が必要な局面ではない」と語った。春期労使交渉で３年連続５％台の賃上げを実現し、２０２５年度の国内の民間企業設備投資は１２８兆円と過去最高水準に達したとし、「企業が投資する、賃金が上がる、消費が伸びるという成長の好循環の道に踏み出せるかどうかの分岐点に立っている」とも指摘した。

金融政策については日銀の判断を尊重すると発言。高市内閣の看板政策である総額３７０兆円超の官民投資による成長戦略はリフレ政策ではないとの認識を示した。官民の投資比率については決まっていないと述べた。

一部企業の負担増が懸念されている非上場株の評価見直しは「現時点で方向性は全く決まっていない」とし、「ゼロベースで検討を進める」と答えた。

＜２年後の消費税、大規模災害発生なら臨機応変に＞

２年間に限定し、その後は税率を戻すとしている飲食料品の消費税減税に関し、大規模災害や感染症などが発生した場合には臨機応変に判断すると述べた。

道路予算の削減発言で批判を浴びている簗和生農水相については「私自身その発言は不適切と考えた」とした上で、「襟を正して職責を全うしてほしい。働いて仕事で返せと言っている」と続投させる考えを示した。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：消費減税、宙に浮く財源　成長投資・防衛費と「三重苦」の様相 アングル：米の対中抑止後退に警戒感、日本政府・与党　習氏は高市氏批判も 焦点：日銀正常化にハードル、高市政権内に慎重論　今春利上げに陰りも コラム：消費減税と日銀の金融政策、求められる「物価の基調」の再定義＝井上哲也氏 焦点：食品消費税ゼロへ本腰、「財源探し」本格化　外為特会頼みの過去 最終更新: 10/8(木) 15:23 ロイター

item.title: Proteinmaxxing is puny remedy for consumer giants
item.description: Groups like PepsiCo and Kraft Heinz are rolling out protein-laced versions of Doritos, mac-and-cheese and even beer. Appealing to health-conscious shoppers helps defend margins as sales shrink. The $56 bln market is still small, though. Little wonder investors remain unconvinced.
item.dc:creator: Aimee Donnellan
item.content:encoded: Walk down any supermarket aisle and you will see a lot of protein. Giant companies like PepsiCo (PEP.O) , Kraft Heinz (KHC.N) and Nestle (NESN.S) have packed the shelves with goodies touting a dose of the nutrient as they attempt to bulk up margins by appealing to health-conscious shoppers. Products including ice cream, Doritos, macaroni and cheese, water and even beer have received a protein boost. But the market is still relatively small and many products are highly processed. The "proteinmaxxing" fad seems unlikely to revive the sickly consumer goods industry. Consumer companies could do with a sales pickup. Soaring energy and commodity prices drove up costs after the pandemic, forcing purveyors of branded goods to raise prices by as much as 10% in one year. Inflation then prompted shoppers to seek out cheaper alternatives. The result is a toxic recipe of declining sales and squeezed margins. Operating profit margins at Danone (DANO.PA) , Nestle, Tyson Foods (TSN.N) , PepsiCo and Kraft Heinz have shrunk by an average of over two percentage points since 2018. The vogue for consuming more protein therefore looks like a saviour to the embattled industry. Aging western populations need it to protect muscle and preserve healthy bones. Doctors advise users of weight-loss drugs to load up on protein to protect lean muscle, which can account for up to 40% of the weight lost from anti-obesity medication. Around 15% of US adults and 3% of the UK population are taking these so-called GLP-1 drugs. Younger, health-obsessed shoppers want to hit their daily protein targets, while parents want more of it for their children. Google searches for “high protein” more than doubled in the five years after the pandemic. Consumer goods giants have responded with a variety of strategies. Nestle is focusing on seasonings that add spice to fresh foods like chicken and fish. Kraft Heinz plans to slap more high-protein labels on the cold cuts and lunch meats it has always sold. But the $26 billion group has also launched PowerMac , a new version of its signature blue-box macaroni and cheese which boasts 17 grams of protein in each serving. Few brands are safe from the proteinmaxxing craze. Mondelez (MDLZ.O) , which sells Philadelphia cream cheese in Europe, has added protein to the dairy spread. PepsiCo introduced Doritos Protein, a variant of its tortilla chips; Kellanova offers protein Pop Tarts . Brewing giant AB InBev (ABI.BR) has launched a protein beer in Brazil that promises 10 grams of the nutrient in each can. Ireland’s Glanbia last year started selling protein water. Changing tastes have also reshaped dealmaking. When Unilever (ULVR.L) in March combined its food division which makes Knorr stock cubes and Hellmann’s mayonnaise with Cholula hot sauce maker McCormick (MKC.N) in a [USN:L6N40J1C6 TEXT:"$66 billion"] deal the two companies said their plan was to create a “global flavour powerhouse”. The thinking was that in a world shaped by weight-loss drugs and young health nuts, selling seasoning for bland chicken fillets offered more growth potential than expanding into snack foods. Carbohydrate-heavy Italian pasta producer Barilla last month agreed to buy Goodles, another purveyor of high-protein mac-and-cheese. Consumer groups are hoping the trend will help them regain some much-needed pricing power. A 48-gram bag of protein-enhanced Doritos costs £2 in the United Kingdom, almost twice as much as a regular packet of the tortilla chips. Similarly, AB InBev’s protein beer is expected to sell for over 10 Brazilian reais, twice the price of a regular bottle of suds. Food and drink companies are betting that consumers that want to boost their protein intake will grab a ready-to-go product when a fresh high-protein meal is not available. However, in many cases these “innovations” are essentially modifications of existing products, which savvy supermarkets can easily replicate with cheaper own-brand alternatives. The arrival of a new breed of highly processed food products may also be a turnoff for consumers. The likes of Kraft Heinz may have more luck with a new range of cleaner label foods, pasta sauces and other products that have fewer ingredients and are less processed. Moreover, higher prices don’t necessarily mean fatter profits, as the protein boom has also pushed up the cost of raw ingredients. In May whey protein concentrate, which is used in shakes and snack bars, hit a record €26,000 a tonne, according to Dutch firm DCA Market Intelligence. The protein market is also relatively small at less than $60 billion last year , according to Towards FnB. Though the research firm expects sales to expand by almost 8% a year, it is too early to tell whether protein is actually moving the dial for Big Food. Kraft Heinz has yet to disclose any sales figures for its new macaroni and cheese and Nestle doesn’t disclose financial details for its division which sells products and seasonings for food cooked in air fryers. PepsiCo has stayed similarly tight-lipped about its protein Doritos. Investors aren’t convinced either. Though the protein vogue offers the prospect of selling consumers more of a product they want at a higher price, the valuation of consumer goods stocks remains depressed. PepsiCo is trading at 14 times expected earnings for the next twelve months, down from nearly 20 times in 2024, according to LSEG. Similarly, Tyson Foods was trading at nearly 16 times forward earnings two years ago and is now valued at just 12 times. The era of proteinmaxxing is unlikely to revive consumer groups’ shrivelled prospects. Follow Aimee Donnellan on LinkedIn .

item.title: Thai consumer confidence drops in September, survey shows
item.description: Thailand's consumer confidence index dropped for the first time in four months in September, hurt by flooding, a slow economic recovery and high living costs, a survey showed on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Thailand's consumer confidence index dropped for the first time in four months in September, hurt by flooding, a slow economic recovery and high living costs, a survey showed on Thursday. The consumer confidence index (THCONF=ECI) of the University of the Thai Chamber of Commerce fell to 52.1 in September from 53.2 in August, it said. Late last month, Bangkok's governor declared the capital a [USN:L6N45I01O TEXT:"disaster-affected"] zone after nearly 300 mm (12 inches) of rain swamped the city in just three days, as much as it typically receives in the whole of September. Economic damage from the floods is estimated at 22 billion baht to 30 billion baht ($655 million to $893 million), and could remain within that range if conditions start to improve next week, Thanavath Phonvichai, the university's president, told a briefing. Global tensions also weighed on confidence in the economy, the university said. Sentiment could improve later this year if flood risks ease, oil prices fall, tourism picks up and government stimulus measures gain traction, the university said. The economy is expected to grow by 2.2% to 2.5% this year, Thanavath said. Southeast Asia's second-largest economy [USN:L6N44E04H TEXT:"expanded"] 2.4% last year, lagging peers. ($1 = 33.61 baht)

item.title: 米、ミャンマー軍政と直接協議開始 孤立化政策を転換
item.description:
Simon Lewis
[ワシントン ８日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Simon Lewis

[ワシントン ８日 ロイター] - トランプ米政権がミャンマー軍事政権と直接協議を始めたことが分かった。協議に詳しい米政府当局者らが明らかにした。２０２１年のクーデター後、国軍指導部の孤立化を図ってきた米国の方針を大きく転換する動きとなる。

協議は米国人を標的とする詐欺拠点の閉鎖に重点を置いているが、ミャンマーのレアアース（希土類）鉱床を含め、より幅広い関与につながる可能性がある。マイケル・バンス米国務次官補（情報調査担当）が軍政との接触で主導的な役割を果たしたという。

バンス氏は９月１５─１６日にミャンマーの首都ネピドーで、クーデター指導者から大統領となったミンアウンフライン氏との協議に参加した。会談は米国人実業家アダム・カスティージョ氏の解放を目的としたものだったが、さらなる関与への糸口にもなったと、関係者らは述べた。

９月の会談はクーデター以降で最高位の接触で、民主化の推進から取引を重視する関与へと軸足を移すトランプ政権の外交政策全般の傾向を浮き彫りにしている。

国務省の情報部門トップとして８月に承認されたバンス氏の協議参加や、同氏の対ミャンマー政策における継続的な役割についてはこれまで報じられていなかった。

前国軍最高司令官のミンアウンフライン氏は、人権侵害を理由に引き続き米国の制裁対象となっている。これには、米政府がジェノサイド（民族大量虐殺）と認定した２０１６─１７年のイスラム教徒少数民族ロヒンギャに対する大量殺害と数十万人の追放が含まれる。国連人権当局者によると、バンス氏の訪問から約２週間後、ミャンマー国軍はラカイン州の混雑した市場を空爆し、５０人超が死亡、さらに数十人が負傷した。

米国務省は、米国の利益に関わる問題についてミャンマーの全ての勢力と接触し、暴力の停止と政治犯の釈放の必要性を提起していると説明した。

item.title: Alcaraz, Sinner among stars locked in for Australian Open 1 Point Slam
item.description: Top professionals take on amateurs for a million-dollar payday ahead of the Grand Slam.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Defending Australian Open champion Carlos Alcaraz will headline the popular AO 1 Point Slam alongside Jannik Sinner, Coco Gauff and Naomi Osaka next year as top professionals take on amateurs again for a million-dollar payday ahead of the Grand Slam. The event, part of the Australian Open's opening week, sees professionals and amateurs battle in a knockout contest where a game of 'Rock, Paper, Scissors' decides who serves or receives and one point is enough to send a player through. It proved hugely popular among fans after its introduction at the 2025 tournament, with some of the amateurs toppling more fancied opponents, before Australian professional Omar Jasika pocketed the inaugural A$60,000 ($41,736) prize. This year, Sydney amateur Jordan Smith bagged A$1 million after beating Taiwan professional Joanna Garland in the final, having also downed Sinner and Amanda Anisimova earlier. "The AO 1 Point Slam is unlike anything else in world sport," the Australian Open's Chief Tennis Officer Tom Larner said in a statement. "It creates an opportunity for grassroots tennis players to share the spotlight with some of the biggest names in the game and delivers a level of excitement that only the Australian Open can provide." At the Australian Open launch in Melbourne on Thursday, organisers said amateur players across the nation were competing in qualifying events at local clubs. The 2027 champion will receive a signature AO 1 Point Slam trophy crafted from Australian silver, they added. The final of the tournament takes place on January 13 at Rod Laver Arena. The Australian Open main draw will run from January 17 to 31. ($1 = 1.4376 Australian dollars)

item.title: Rays, benefiting from fan-interference call, complete sweep of Yankees
item.description: NEW YORK -- Rookie Victor Mesa Jr. belted a tiebreaking two-run homer in the sixth inning and the Tampa Bay Rays earned a 4-3 victory over the New York Yankees on Wednesday to complete a three-game sweep of their American League Division Series.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: NEW YORK -- Rookie Victor Mesa Jr. belted a tiebreaking two-run homer in the sixth inning and the Tampa Bay Rays earned a 4-3 victory over the New York Yankees on Wednesday to complete a three-game sweep of their American League Division Series. The Rays are headed to the AL Championship Series for the third time in club history and will host the Chicago White Sox or Cleveland Guardians in a best-of-seven series that begins Monday. "The way our pitchers just executed multiple times through that lineup was really, really impressive, but we did it for the most part by just limiting walks," Rays manager Kevin Cash said. "If you don't walk them, you're going to give yourself a chance." Tampa Bay also celebrated at Yankee Stadium for the second time this season after clinching the AL East title with a 6-1 win over the Yankees on Sept. 22. The Yankees were thwarted in part by a fan-interference call that overturned a potential game-tying homer from Anthony Volpe in the bottom of the sixth. New York starter Max Fried (1-1) quickly got the first two outs of the sixth but allowed a single to Junior Caminero that whizzed over the left-hander's head and past second baseman Volpe's diving attempt behind the bag on the outfield grass. On the next pitch, Mesa crushed a sweeper into the right-center-field seats for his first career postseason homer. "(Once) I hit it, I knew it was going out," Mesa said. "When you don't even feel the bat, that means that you got good contact. And just blessed to be here and help the team. That's my goal is (to) help the team, defense, offense, whatever it is to get the win." It was the second big play Mesa made in the series after his strong throw from right field led to Austin Wells being thrown out at third in the eighth inning in Game 1 on Saturday. Tampa Bay's Jonathan Aranda delivered an RBI single in the third and Ryan Vilade hit a homer that just cleared the right field fence in the fourth. Ben Rice had an RBI single in the third and Spencer Jones hit an RBI double in the fourth, but the Yankees were swept in a division series for the first time in team history. New York lost in the ALDS for the fourth time in nine seasons under manager Aaron Boone and 11th time in team history. "I thought we had some good at-bats tonight," Boone said. "Gave ourselves some opportunities, hit some balls on the screws again, but ultimately not enough. We gotta be more complete offensively, defensively, pitching. We did a lot of really good things this year, but ultimately not good enough to beat a really good Rays team tonight." Volpe nearly hit a tying two-run homer with two outs in the sixth off Griffin Jax, but a fan reached over the left field fence and the ball caromed off the spectator's palm. Volpe was originally awarded a home run, but following a crew-chief review, he was placed on second with an RBI double. Volpe said, "(I was) just seeing it through the replay and just hoping for the best, but ... crazy." After going 5-for-58 in the first two games, New York made a few tweaks to its struggling order. Trent Grisham batted leadoff while Volpe replaced Jazz Chisholm Jr. at second base and Jose Caballero replaced Ryan McMahon at third. Grisham went 0-for-5 with three strikeouts. Volpe finished 2-for-4, and Caballero went 0-for-2. Tampa Bay's Nick Martinez allowed two runs on five hits in 3 2/3 innings. He exited after Volpe's comebacker hit him on the lower back. Ian Seymour (1-0) followed Martinez with 1 1/3 scoreless innings. Jax tossed two innings, allowing the run on Volpe's overturned homer. Cam Booser got the first two outs of the eighth before Kevin Kelly struck out pinch hitter Giancarlo Stanton. Bryan Baker stranded a runner in the ninth to notch his third save of the series by striking out Grisham on a changeup. Fried allowed four runs on seven hits in 5 2/3 innings. He fanned seven without issuing a walk. --Larry Fleisher, Field Level Media

item.title: Indonesia industrial parks to waive land rental fees to attract investment, Danantara says
item.description: Indonesian state-owned industrial parks will waive land rental fees from next year to attract foreign investors, the chief operating officer of sovereign wealth fund Danantara Indonesia said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indonesian state-owned industrial parks will waive land rental fees from next year to attract foreign investors, the chief operating officer of sovereign wealth fund Danantara Indonesia said on Thursday. To cover the cost of the waiver, the parks will seek to earn revenue from facilities fees, such as electricity, water treatment and fibre optics, COO Dony Oskaria said Danantara, which oversees all Indonesian state-owned enterprises, has been tasked with increasing investment inflows to help reach President Prabowo Subianto's target of 8% economic growth by 2029 The announcement comes ahead of Danantara's planned merger of 23 state industrial park operators into a single entity next month, something it has done in other sectors to increase [USN:P8N3T007L TEXT:"efficiency"] The new entity will become the "largest industrial estate in Southeast Asia" with around 35,000 hectares (86,500 acres) of land under management, Dony said

item.title: India FX forward premiums extend post-RBI policy surge; 1-year up 64 bps this week
item.description: India's FX forward premiums extended their post-policy surge on Thursday, with the one-year implied rate now up 64 basis points this week on expectations that the central bank could conduct more sell/buy swaps, while high overnight swap costs add to upward pressure.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's FX forward premiums extended their post-policy surge on Thursday, with the one-year implied rate now up 64 basis points this week on expectations that the central bank could conduct more sell/buy swaps, while high overnight swap costs add to upward pressure. The 1-year implied rate rose 11 basis points to 3.94%, following a 36-bps surge on Wednesday following the Reserve Bank of India's policy decision.

item.title: Morning Bid: Sovereign bonds shouldered aside as AI takes their turf
item.description: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Wayne Cole
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Wayne Cole Sovereign borrowers are no longer the big boys on the block as AI giants increasingly invade their turf. The [USN:FWN45T25Y TEXT:"Wall Street Journal"] reports Broadcom (AVGO.O) is lining up $50 billion of financing to buy gear from OpenAI, with Oracle (ORCL.N) also seeking an unspecified sum. Sources say [USN:L6N45S1CR TEXT:"SpaceX"] (SPCX.O) alone is looking to issue $30 billion in investment-grade debt, along with a cool $10 billion in bank loans, to buy chips from Nvidia (NVDA.O) . This is the same SpaceX that raised a record $86 billion in its June IPO and then immediately sold $25 billion in bonds. Nvidia also happens to hold a stake worth around $21 billion in the Elon Musk venture. Some analysts saw this as a wise move by Musk as it could help SpaceX steal a march in the AI arms race, which is all about who gets to scale first. Using debt also means not having to go back to the equity market and diluting stock. Others worried about the circular nature of all this business, with the chipmakers helping fund the buyers of their own products. Investors also seemed to have qualms about turning equity risk into credit risk, as SpaceX's five-year CDS spread widened almost 15 basis points to a record. That hyperscalers are bold enough to raise such momentous sums should be music to the ears of companies that make all this data-centre gear. [USN:L1N45T115 TEXT:"Samsung"] (005930.KS) today projected a nearly nine-fold increase in operating profit to $80 billion, though its shares still slipped 1.3%. Whatever the business merits, all this corporate borrowing is a real headache for governments that need to fund persistent budget deficits and increased defence spending in a more uncertain world. All as ageing populations demand more healthcare and pension payments, while shrinking the tax base. Problems [USN:L8N45S0RJ TEXT:"France"] knows all too well. It's never a good sign when your [USN:L8N45T074 TEXT:"central bank governor"] has to reassure investors the country does not need help from that big bank in Frankfurt. The prospect of increasing competition from corporate borrowers saw yields on 10-year Treasuries edge back up to 5.31% in Asia. Yields had fallen from a top of 5.3645% overnight when the latest note auction drew so much demand the Street was left holding hardly any of the paper. Now, it's time for the 30-year to step into the limelight and see if yields around 5.70% can draw the same sort of bids. Key developments that could influence markets on Thursday: - German trade balance for August - Fed speakers include Governor Christopher Waller, Fed Bank of Minneapolis President Neel Kashkari and Fed Bank of St. Louis President Alberto Musalem - Various appearances by SNB Vice President Antoine Martin, BoE Chief Economist Huw Pill, BoE policymaker Clare Lombardelli, ECB chief economist Philip Lane, Norges Bank Governor Ida Wolden Bache, Riksbank Governor Erik Thedéen

item.title: Vietnam says its trade deal negotiations with US are largely completed
item.description: Vietnam's government said its negotiations with the United States on a reciprocal trade agreement have largely been completed after seven rounds of talks since April 2025.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Vietnam's government said its negotiations with the United States on a reciprocal trade agreement have largely been completed after seven rounds of talks since April 2025. The two sides have "basically completed almost all negotiating contents" and are now working through a handful of remaining technical issues, Ngo Chung Khanh, a trade ministry official, was cited as saying in a statement issued late on Wednesday Close coordination with US agencies was expected, particularly the Office of the US Trade Representative, to finalise remaining issues and pave the way for the deal's signing and implementation, it said Vietnam's trade surplus with the US reached $122.62 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 23.8% from a year earlier, according to Vietnam's National Statistics Office [USN:L6N45E00M TEXT:"Vietnamese leader To Lam"] last month said negotiations on a trade agreement between the two countries had been positive and a deal could be signed soon

item.title: South Korea may ban foreign banks arranging global bond deals, Bloomberg News reports
item.description: South Korea is considering regulations to prohibit investment banks without domestic securities licenses from seeking to arrange overseas bond sales of local issuers, Bloomberg News reported on Wednesday citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korea is considering regulations to prohibit investment banks without domestic securities licenses from seeking to arrange overseas bond sales of local issuers, Bloomberg News reported on Wednesday citing people familiar with the matter. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

item.title: 米、同盟国に偽情報対策会議への支持取り下げ要請 対米批判パネル理由に
item.description: [ワシントン ７日 ロイター] - 米国務省がカナダや欧州の同盟国に対し、「偽情報対策会議
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ワシントン ７日 ロイター] - 米国務省がカナダや欧州の同盟国に対し、「偽情報対策会議 」への支持を取り下げるよう働きかけていたことが分かった。同会議に、米国が欧州にとって情報面の脅威になっているとの見方を検証するパネル討論が含まれていることが理由。事情に詳しい米政府当局者３人の話と、ロイターが確認した関連文書で明らかになった。

偽情報対策会議はブリュッセルに本拠を置く非営利団体「ＥＵディスインフォラボ」が主催。７─８日の日程でリトアニアの首都ビリニュスで開催されている。

米政府当局者らによると、国務省は数日間にわたり、リトアニア、カナダ、フランスのカウンターパートに同会議の件で働きかけた。説得を受け、会議の「主要支援者」として記載されていたカナダとリトアニアの外務省は、会議から距離を置いたという。

欧州連合（ＥＵ）の対外行動庁（外務省に相当）も会議の支援者リストから姿を消したが、ロイターは国務省が接触したかどうかを確認できなかった。

仏政府は現在も、会議唯一の「主要支援者」として記載されている。

問題のパネル討論は「米国はいかにして欧州にとってのＦＩＭＩ（外国からの情報操作・干渉）上の脅威となったのか」をテーマとする予定。

item.title: India considers delaying UPI payment fee rollout, sources say
item.description: India is considering delaying the rollout of a fee on large payments via its popular Unified Payments Interface platform by a few months, according to a regulatory official and an industry executive familiar with the discussions.
item.dc:creator: Ashwin Manikandan, Ira Dugal
item.content:encoded: India is considering delaying the rollout of a fee on large payments via its popular Unified Payments Interface platform by a few months, according to a regulatory official and an industry executive familiar with the discussions. India last month ended more than six years of [USN:L4N4570YD TEXT:"zero-cost payments"] by announcing a 0.4% charge for merchants on transactions exceeding 2,000 rupees ($21), [USN:L4N4580NI TEXT:"drawing opposition"] from retailers and a large broker. UPI is used by over 500 million people to buy everything from roadside cups of tea to iPhones in Asia's third-largest economy. Walmart's (WMT.O) PhonePe and Alphabet's (GOOGL.O) GooglePay had about 80% market share by value of UPI transactions in August. The fee, set to come into effect from October 15, would have coincided with India's annual festive season that runs from October through December and typically sees a surge in consumer spending. A final decision on delaying the rollout has yet to be taken by the National Payments Corporation of India but is expected in the coming days, one of the sources said. A delay in implementation would allow payments firms to upgrade systems and not pass on costs to customers, while addressing issues retailers may face during the festive period, the sources said, requesting anonymity as the discussions are private. The fee could kick in from January, the industry executive said. An email to the NPCI was not answered. Moneycontrol first reported the likely delay. Stocks of Indian digital payments firms slid on Thursday as these companies would benefit from the charge. Paytm (PAYT.NS) and Mobikwik (ONEM.NS) dropped 5.5% and 7%, respectively, while Pine Labs (PINL.NS) slid 3%.

item.title: 中国、ＥＵのハイブリッド車輸出自主規制要請を拒否＝ＦＴ
item.description: [７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[７日 ロイター] - 英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（ＦＴ）は７日、中国が欧州連合（ＥＵ）によるハイブリッド車（ＨＶ）の輸出自主規制要請を拒否したと報じた。双方は貿易紛争回避に向けた交渉の最終局面に入っている。

ＦＴが外交筋２人の話として伝えたところによると、欧州委員会はこれを受け、代わりにＨＶ輸入に上限を設けるＥＵの一方的な措置を中国政府に受け入れさせたい考えだという。

item.title: Bollywood actor Nana Patekar dies at 75
item.description: Nana Patekar, a veteran Indian actor known for his fiery performances in Bollywood films and theatre, died on Thursday aged 75, local media reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nana Patekar, a veteran Indian actor known for his fiery performances in Bollywood films and theatre, died on Thursday aged 75, local media reported. Patekar was found unconscious at his home in the coastal state of Goa early on Thursday morning and doctors were unable to revive him, news agency ANI and other media reported. He died of cardiac arrest, but it was unclear what triggered it, Shekhar Salkar, chief of the oncology department at the Manipal Hospital, where Patekar was brought, told ANI. Born Vishawanath Patekar, but popularly known as Nana, he started his career doing theatre in Marathi, the language spoken in his home state of Maharashtra, which is also home to Bollywood. Patekar acted in several of India's arthouse movies in the 1970's and 80's, including Mira Nair's award-winning "Salaam Bombay" before moving to mainstream Bollywood. He played a variety of roles, sharing screen space with actors such as Amitabh Bachchan and Shah Rukh Khan and excelling in both serious and comic roles. His performances, marked by trademark aggression and forceful dialogue, won him several national and regional film awards. "He was one of those rare actors who never needed to do too much to make you sit up and watch. That voice, that intensity, that honesty in every performance...he was completely his own," said actor Akshay Kumar, who acted with Patekar in several movies. Patekar is survived by his wife, from whom he was separated, and a son.

item.title: ホルムズ海峡通過船、2カ月超ぶり低水準 タンカー攻撃増加で
item.description:
Florence Tan
[シンガポール ８日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Florence Tan

[シンガポール ８日 ロイター] - ホルムズ海峡を通航する船舶数が２カ月余りぶりの低水準に落ち込んだことが、船舶追跡データで分かった。同海峡でのタンカーへの攻撃は先週、米国とイスラエルによる対イラン戦争の開始以降で最多となった。

分析会社ケプラーのデータによると、６日に同海峡を通航したコモディティー（商品）輸送船は７隻と、７月２３日以来の低水準だった。

ケプラーのアナリストは１０月６日付のリポートで、「海峡を通過する原油の量は、戦争開始以降で最高を記録した前週から２７％減少し、日量で少なくとも１０１０万バレルとなった」と記した。

「９月の平均水準に戻ったが、戦争前の７４％の水準だ」とした。

減少の大半は、船舶間で積み荷を移し替える瀬取り（ＳＴＳ）がオマーン湾で減ったことによるものだったという。

一方、オマーン湾沿岸と紅海からの輸出は戦争前の２倍超に当たる日量６７０万バレルに増加し、ホルムズ海峡経由の供給減を補った。これにより、中東産原油の輸出全体は戦争前の水準を維持したという。

データによると、７日に海峡を通航した船舶数は１０隻に小幅に増加したが、４日と５日のそれぞれ２０隻超を大幅に下回った。

過去２日間は、海峡に入った船舶数が出た船舶数を上回った。

これらの集計には、探知を避けるため船舶自動識別装置を切って通航する船舶は含まれていない。

item.title: トルコ、サウジに防衛・技術支援 フーシ派対応で＝当局者
item.description:
Tuvan Gumrukcu Timour Azhari
[アンカラ／リヤド ７日 ロイター] - トルコがイエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派と戦うサウジアラビアに対し、主に防衛・技術面の支援を提供していると、当局者２人が７日明らかにした。
トルコ、パキスタン、サウジアラビアは８月、「メッカ共同防衛協定」に署名した。加盟国のいずれか１カ国に対する武力攻撃は３カ国全てに対する攻撃と見なすと定めている。
３カ国は５日、共同防衛義務を直ちに履行し、サウジに迅速に部隊を展開することで合意した。
トルコはフーシ派によるサウジ攻撃を非難し、
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Tuvan Gumrukcu　Timour Azhari

[アンカラ／リヤド ７日 ロイター] - トルコがイエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派と戦うサウジアラビアに対し、主に防衛・技術面の支援を提供していると、当局者２人が７日明らかにした。

トルコ、パキスタン、サウジアラビアは８月、「メッカ共同防衛協定」に署名した。加盟国のいずれか１カ国に対する武力攻撃は３カ国全てに対する攻撃と見なすと定めている。

３カ国は５日、共同防衛義務を直ちに履行し、サウジに迅速に部隊を展開することで合意した。

トルコはフーシ派によるサウジ攻撃を非難し、 サウジの軍事技術面のニーズに応える意向を示すとともに、紅海の航行の安全確保に向けたサウジ主導の連合に参加することに合意した。

匿名を条件に取材に応じたトルコ当局者は、トルコに期待されている支援は軍事装備品の提供、情報共有、兵器システムの提供に限られるとし、この同盟の一環として他の形態の派遣・配備はこれまで行われていないと述べた。

当局者らによると、トルコ議会が共同防衛協定を正式に批准していないため、防空システムを含むサウジへの支援は当面、主に２国間の枠組みで行われる。批准後には支援の規模と内容が拡大する見通しだという。

状況説明を受けた米当局者は、トルコがこれまでに戦略立案支援や兵たん支援など、おおむね防衛的な能力の提供を決めたと述べた。ドローン操縦者の派遣や、防衛措置の微調整支援のほか、情報収集・監視・偵察が含まれるという。

トルコのフィダン外相は５日、サウジの首都リヤドで開かれたメッカ防衛協定の緊急会合後、国営メディアに対し、サウジの防衛能力を支えるためにどのような支援を提供するかを協議したと説明。 「国防相と参謀総長も同席し、特に軍事、作戦、技術面の問題について非常に有益な見解を示した」と述べた。

パキスタンや地域の当局者らはこれまでに、トルコとパキスタンがサウジに対し、イエメンで使用する軍事装備を提供していると述べていた。

イエメン暫定政府軍は今週、サウジ主導の連合による航空支援を受け、紅海の要衝バベルマンデブ海峡周辺地域の奪還に向けて反転攻勢を開始した。

item.title: Malaysia to work towards Myanmar's full reintegration into ASEAN, PM says
item.description: Malaysia's Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said his government would do "whatever possible" to ensure Myanmar was re-integrated into the Southeast Asian bloc ASEAN, following a meeting with Myanmar's military-backed leader Min Aung Hlaing on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Rozanna Latiff
item.content:encoded: Malaysia's Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said his government would do "whatever possible" to ensure Myanmar was re-integrated into the Southeast Asian bloc ASEAN, following a meeting with Myanmar's military-backed leader Min Aung Hlaing on Thursday. Anwar also pledged to continue working with Myanmar, including on the [USN:L6N45L0GD TEXT:"repatriation"] of thousands of Myanmar nationals from Malaysia - a move that has been widely [USN:L6N45M0GV TEXT:"criticised"] by the United Nations and rights groups concerned about the risks from an ongoing civil war. Former Myanmar junta chief Min Aung Hlaing is on a [USN:L6N45T0KC TEXT:"two-day visit"] to Malaysia as he seeks greater international legitimacy after [USN:L6N40M04J TEXT:"becoming"] president in April following an [USN:L6N3YV0LH TEXT:"election"] that Western nations and rights groups widely criticised as a sham. Myanmar has been in turmoil since 2021 when Min Aung Hlaing led a military coup against a democratically elected government, triggering armed conflict across much of the country. Min Aung Hlaing and other senior Myanmar officials have been barred from attending summits of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) after failing to adhere to an ASEAN-brokered peace plan following the coup, but some member countries have sought to re-establish ties. Since becoming president, Min Aung Hlaing has also visited ASEAN members [USN:L6N44305P TEXT:"Thailand"], Laos, Cambodia and Vietnam. Malaysia's Anwar acknowledged ongoing concerns about democratic processes in Myanmar but said differences must be respected, adding that Min Aung Hlaing had shown a willingness to be collaborative. "I would say that we and our part in Malaysia, will do whatever is possible to make sure that we enhance this collaboration and ultimately, take Myanmar as part of our community of nations, without prejudice, and particularly in the context of ASEAN," Anwar told a media briefing following the meeting. MYANMAR TO SEND MORE NAVY SHIPS TO REPATRIATE ITS CITIZENS Anwar also expressed appreciation to Min Aung Hlaing for accepting the repatriation of 10,493 Myanmar nationals from Malaysia so far. Malaysia has said it can no longer take in refugees from Myanmar, saying they had become a financial burden and a security risk. Malaysia is not a party to the UN refugee convention and treats asylum-seekers as illegal migrants. The country last month [USN:L6N45L084 TEXT:"sent back"] around 1,500 people on Myanmar naval ships, part of a wider repatriation programme that could see as many as 5,000 people deported. Min Aung Hlaing said at Thursday's briefing Myanmar citizens currently held at Malaysian immigration detention centres would be brought back as soon as possible. "Because the current weather is favourable, I will dispatch navy ships to repatriate them," he said, adding that he would formally request Malaysia to allow the repatriation. He also extended an invitation for Anwar to visit Myanmar "when the time is right". Anwar and Min Aung Hlaing did not mention if their discussions included plans to repatriate Rohingya Muslim refugees, many of whom fled Myanmar after a brutal 2017 military crackdown in the country's Rakhine state that is now the subject of a genocide case at the International Court of Justice. Muslim-majority Malaysia widely criticised the crackdown at the time. But public sentiment has turned in recent years, with the Rohingya in Malaysia facing increasing [USN:L6N43T0QE TEXT:"harassment and scrutiny"], amid [USN:L6N43F0LG TEXT:"a surge"] of online hate speech and misinformation. Anwar has said he would push for Myanmar to accept Rohingya refugees. There are more than 193,000 refugees and asylum seekers from Myanmar in Malaysia, about 65% of them Rohingya, according to the UN refugee agency. Buddhist-majority Myanmar does not recognise the Rohingya as one of its official ethnic groups and denies citizenship to most.

item.title: Britain removes East Jerusalem consulate signage as Israeli shutdown deadline expires
item.description: Workers removed signs and plaques at the British consulate in East Jerusalem overnight after Israel ordered it shut by Thursday over London's plans to impose sanctions on settlements in the West Bank, further damaging strained ties between allies.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Cornwell, Ammar Awad
item.content:encoded: Workers removed signs and plaques at the British consulate in East Jerusalem overnight after Israel ordered it shut by Thursday over London's plans to impose [USN:S8N42N05Y TEXT:"sanctions"] on settlements in the West Bank, further damaging strained ties between allies. Reuters journalists saw workers in the consulate remove a plaque reading "British Consulate General" and another sign for its consular section. The British flag was still flying over the building. There was no immediate comment from the consulate. Israel last month ordered Britain to close the consulate within [USN:S8N44F000 TEXT:"30 days"] and remove its diplomats from the city, after Britain announced sanctions targeting Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, including a trade ban on goods made there. The United Nations and most countries consider the settlements to be illegal under international law. Israel disputes this. Israel has been adamant the consulate will close even as Britain sought to keep it open, including [USN:L8N45R0TE TEXT:"sending"] the country's top national security adviser to Israel last week for talks. Britain's presence in the city dates back almost 200 years, long before the State of Israel was established in 1948. The closure order does not affect Britain's embassy in Tel Aviv, which handles diplomatic relations with Israel's government. The consulate, in the Sheikh Jarrah neighbourhood of East Jerusalem, handles Britain's relations with Palestinians in Jerusalem, as well as in the West Bank and Gaza. It also provides consular services to Palestinians. Britain's Foreign Office on Wednesday declined to comment when asked whether the consulate was still operating or any British diplomats working there had returned to the UK. Sources have said the order to close the consulate affects around 30 British diplomats along with their family members. Britain is [USN:L8N45S07O TEXT:"considering"] expelling Israeli diplomats from Israel's embassy in the United Kingdom in response to any closure of the consulate, Reuters reported on Tuesday, citing sources. It would be a highly unusual step for the allies to expel each other's diplomats. Despite the current strains, the UK and Israel are close economic, security and intelligence partners. The British sanctions announcement, and Israel's order to close the consulate, mark a new low in a relationship that has deteriorated over the past three years. Britain has repeatedly criticised Israel over its actions in the war in Gaza and over Israeli settler attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank. Benjamin Netanyahu's government has accused Britain's governing Labour Party of being hostile towards Israel.

item.title: US opens direct talks with Myanmar's generals, reversing years of isolation
item.description: The Trump administration has begun direct talks with Myanmar’s military-installed government in a sharp reversal of Washington's efforts to isolate the country’s generals after the 2021 coup.
item.dc:creator: Simon Lewis
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration has begun direct talks with Myanmar’s military-installed government, according to US officials and others familiar with the outreach, in a sharp reversal of Washington's efforts to isolate the country’s generals after the 2021 coup. The US Assistant Secretary of State for Intelligence and Research, Michael Vance, played a leading role in the outreach, which has focused on shutting down [USN:L3N3PM029 TEXT:"scam centers"] that target Americans but could lead to broader engagement, including on Myanmar’s rare-earth mineral deposits, according to seven current and former officials and others familiar with the policy shift. Vance joined talks with coup leader-turned-president Min Aung Hlaing in the capital Naypyitaw on September 15-16. The meeting was aimed at securing the release of American businessman Adam Castillo but also provided an opening for further engagement, four of the people said. Last month’s meeting — the highest‑level contact since the coup — underscores a broader Trump‑administration foreign policy tilt away from democracy promotion toward transactional engagement. The presence of Vance, who was confirmed as the State Department’s top intelligence official in August, and his ongoing role in US policy toward Myanmar have not been previously reported. MILITARY LEADER REMAINS UNDER US SANCTIONS Min Aung Hlaing, the former military chief, remains under US sanctions for human rights abuses, including the 2016-2017 mass killings and expulsions of hundreds of thousands of Rohingya Muslims that Washington [USN:S0N2TK07R TEXT:"declared a genocide"]. Less than two weeks after Vance’s visit, Myanmar’s military conducted an [USN:L1N45L0X3 TEXT:"airstrike on a crowded marketplace"] in Rakhine state, killing [USN:L4N45L0JH TEXT:"over 50 people"] and injuring scores more, according to United Nations human rights officials. The State Department said it engages with all groups in Myanmar on issues affecting US interests and raises the need to cease violence and release political prisoners. “You don't solve problems by ignoring them. You solve problems by addressing them,” spokesperson Tommy Pigott said in a statement. A spokesperson for the military-backed government did not respond to a request for comment. Min Aung Hlaing, who has cited electoral fraud to justify the coup and labeled his opponents as terrorists, is [USN:L4N45S0XZ TEXT:"seeking international legitimacy"] for his nominally civilian government. Current and former officials say Vance has met players from all sides of Myanmar’s complex conflict and helped shape the Trump administration’s policy toward the country. Intelligence chiefs — such as Vance — do not typically steer policy because of concerns about compromising analytic independence. “If you let policy dictate to intelligence, you can't be sure you're getting a real honest assessment of the facts,” said Richard Betts, an adjunct senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations who has consulted for US intelligence agencies. Pigott declined to address Vance’s role but said the administration “operates as a team with the president as the lead.” A DETAINED AMERICAN, AND AN OPENING Castillo, a former head of the American Chamber of Commerce in Myanmar, was detained at Yangon airport on June 11 by Myanmar authorities on what his supporters have described as trumped-up charges. The US government has not commented on whether Castillo was wrongfully detained. People familiar with the matter said White House, National Security Council and State Department officials held back-channel negotiations with Myanmar officials to secure his release. One person said Myanmar asked only "to have an official engagement at the right level with the US government" in return. Castillo declined to comment beyond crediting President Donald Trump for his release. The meeting builds on a June meeting between US and Myanmar officials in Tokyo also involving Vance, four people said. One of the people said officials from the Treasury Department, which oversees sanctions, the Department of Homeland Security, and the Pentagon took part. It was unclear who represented Myanmar at the talks. Vance, who became involved in Myanmar policy while advising Vice President JD Vance on Asian affairs, has also met in person and virtually with the democratic opposition and ethnic armed groups fighting the military, five of the people said. A major focus of the US push is getting Myanmar's help shuttering [USN:L6N43N05M TEXT:"scam hubs"] [USN:L4N3WX0H9 TEXT:"operating on its territory"] that run romance and other frauds , which have scammed Americans out of [USN:L3N3UW09U TEXT:"billions of dollars"]. Two people familiar with the matter said the FBI has had direct contact with Myanmar’s authorities on cyber scams. Researchers say many scams are run from areas under militia control, with some proceeds flowing to the military, raising doubts about whether Myanmar’s leaders are serious about enforcement. US officials also [USN:L1N3TM0L0 TEXT:"discussed access"] to Myanmar’s massive deposits of heavy rare earths that are used in electric vehicles and wind turbines. US officials acknowledge obstacles: the deposits mainly lie in [USN:L4N41Y099 TEXT:"territory held by ethnic armies"] fighting Myanmar’s military government, and China, currently the main importer, could see any US role as a challenge. Still, with Washington seeking to diversify supply chains away from China, Myanmar's deposits remain a recurring topic in conversations, the people said. FROM SANCTIONS TO ENGAGEMENT After the 2021 coup, President Joe Biden's administration [USN:KCN2AW2MC TEXT:"froze Myanmar's assets"] at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and imposed sanctions on [USN:W1N2JA01P TEXT:"senior officers"] and military‑linked[USN:L4N38D162 TEXT:" businesses."] In 2022, Congress authorized non-lethal support for the opposition, funding early-warning systems for airstrikes and incentives for officers to defect. Most of those programs were cut during Trump’s foreign-aid overhaul last year, according to four current and former officials and State Department correspondence with Congress reviewed by Reuters. The State Department said its engagement with the military government does not diminish its relationships with other groups. The US continues to provide assistance to areas outside military control, it said, without detailing that aid. Representative Gregory Meeks, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said the shift was “contrary to both our values and our interests.” “By engaging Min Aung Hlaing while failing to implement congressionally mandated sanctions and deploy appropriated democracy funding, Secretary (Marco) Rubio is ceding U.S. leadership and providing this murderous regime greater international legitimacy,” Meeks said in a statement to Reuters. Myanmar's government, installed after elections criticized by rights groups as a sham, has hired lobbyists to press its case in Washington. In April, Roger Stone, a longtime Trump adviser, began consulting for DCI Group on behalf of Myanmar's Ministry of Information, according to Foreign Agents Registration Act filings. Stone was convicted in 2019 of obstructing a congressional investigation into Russian interference in the 2016 election. Trump later pardoned him. A newsletter distributed by DCI warned in June that Washington risked being shut out of access to critical minerals if it did not engage with Myanmar. (This story has been refiled to add a missing word in paragraph 2 and fix grammar in paragraph 9.)

item.title: Encroaching energy, mine concessions threaten protected ecosystems, research shows
item.description: Millions of hectares of protected tropical ecosystems are at risk from overlapping mining concessions and oil and gas blocks, researchers said on Thursday, potentially weakening a global treaty aimed at conserving 30% of the world's land, freshwater and oceans by the end of the decade.
item.dc:creator: David Stanway
item.content:encoded: Millions of hectares of protected tropical ecosystems are at risk from overlapping mining concessions and oil and gas blocks, researchers said on Thursday, potentially weakening a global treaty aimed at conserving 30% of the world's land, freshwater and oceans by the end of the decade. The research , led by US environment group Earth Insight, was released ahead of a new round of UN biodiversity talks scheduled to get underway in Yerevan, Armenia on October 18. The COP17 meeting will see the publication of a global "stocktake" showing that existing government commitments were still [USN:L4N45E04F TEXT:"way behind"] what was required to meet the "30x30" pledge. Earth Insight said current pledges would raise conservation levels to 23% by 2030, but reaching the 30% target simply by "counting hectares" would not be enough if many of the areas covered were still vulnerable to industrial development. "To say that a third of the Earth's surface needs to be protected, and for that to be agreed upon by consensus by 196 countries, was a big deal, but the focus has just gone on that quantitative element," said Madhu Rao, chair of the World Commission on Protected Areas at the International Union for Conservation of Nature. Earth Insight used spatial analysis to examine the overlap between major tropical ecosystems and extractive industries, and found that oil and gas blocks encroached on more than 61 million hectares (235,522 square miles), an area nearly the size of France. Mining concessions overlapped with another 42.7 million hectares of protected areas. "A majority of those concessions haven't been licensed yet - certainly plenty are, but that means there's an opportunity for countries to remove those concessions," said Tyson Miller, Earth Insight's executive director. Some of the concessions have already caused damage to national parks across the world, including Cambodia's Phnom Prich wildlife sanctuary, which lost 10,000 hectares to make way for an open-pit gold mine. While 97% of Cambodia's undisturbed tropical forest lies within designated protected zones, 21% is threatened by mining and 71% by oil and gas development. More than 40% of key marine biodiversity areas in the Amazon remain unprotected, with the figure rising beyond 50% in both Southeast Asia and Central America. Earth Insight said its findings were likely to be "conservative" and did not capture the full range of pressures on ecosystems. More concessions could be activated as countries rush to improve energy security, with Bangladesh already inviting companies to [USN:L1N421024 TEXT:"bid for oil blocks"] in biodiversity-rich waters in the Bay of Bengal, Rao said. "Given the energy crisis that we are in at the moment, many countries are taking the steps forward, getting into oil extraction in a way they hadn't done before."

item.title: Isaias intensifies into first Atlantic hurricane of 2026
item.description: Hurricane Isaias became the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season, triggering production shut-ins and evacuations at energy facilities in the US Gulf.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hurricane Isaias became the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season, triggering production shut-ins and evacuations at energy facilities in the US Gulf. Isaias was located about 445 miles (715 Km) south-southwest of the mouth of the Mississippi river, packing maximum sustained winds of 75 mph (120 kph), the US National Hurricane Center said on Thursday. The NHC noted additional strengthening is expected and that Isaias should remain a strong hurricane as it approaches the northern Gulf coast on Friday night. The hurricane is expected to pass through areas with significant offshore [USN:L1N45T0JO TEXT:"oil and gas production"], along with onshore refining facilities, which could pressure inventories and already-high prices at the pump. The strong El Niño weather pattern has limited hurricane formation in the Atlantic this year by creating unfavorable wind conditions that disrupt strengthening storms. US energy companies such as Shell (SHEL.L) and Chevron (CVX.N) [USN:L4N45T1Q7 TEXT:"said"] they were curtailing offshore operations at their Gulf platforms. US Gulf of Mexico oil and gas producers [USN:L4N45T1G2 TEXT:"had shut in"] about 25.08% of current oil production and 16.37% of current natural gas production as of Wednesday, according to the Marine Minerals Administration.

item.title: ペルー中銀、政策金利を4.25％に据え置き 利上げ予想に反し
item.description:
[リマ ７日 ロイター] - ペルー中央銀行は７日、政策金利を４．２５％に据え置いた。天候の影響で国内物価に上昇圧力がかかり、インフレ率が目標レンジを上回る中、アナリストは、金利据え置き局面が終わり２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）の利上げが実施されると予想していた。
• ９月のインフレ率は前年同月比４．５％と、主に燃料価格と電気料金の上昇を背景に８月の４．４％から小幅に加速。食品とエネルギーを除くコアインフレ率は４．５％で横ばいだった。
• ロイターの調査によると、アナリストは、政策金利が４．５０％に引き上げられると予想していた。実施されれば３年余りぶりの利上げとなるはずだった。
• 中銀は、９月の１年先のインフレ期待は３．１％と横ばいで、引き続き目標レンジの上限を若干上回ったと説明。ただ、供給ショックが和らぐにつれ、インフレ率は総合、コアともに、２％に向けて低下するとの見通しを示した。
